name: Isolated Hyperphalangy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Isolated Hyperphalangy

criteria.description: Presence of an additional phalanx in one or more digits confirmed by physical examination
Radiographic evidence of supernumerary phalanx(s) without associated syndromic features
Absence of other congenital anomalies or syndromic features on clinical and genetic evaluation
Family history of isolated hyperphalangy or similar digital anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical digital anomaly with radiographic confirmation of additional phalanx and exclusion of syndromic causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to rule out syndromic associations but is not diagnostic for isolated hyperphalangy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of supernumerary phalanx in one or more digits
Digital lengthening due to additional phalanx
searchTerms: longer fingers due to extra bone
extended finger length from additional bone

common.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of affected digit(s)

searchTerms: finger shape abnormality with no discomfort

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected digit(s)
searchTerms: restricted range of motion in fingers

common.symptomName: Asymmetry in finger or toe length
searchTerms: difference in finger or toe length

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint stiffness in affected digits
Cosmetic concerns related to digital appearance

rare.symptomName: Secondary osteoarthritis in affected digit joints
searchTerms: joint wear and tear in digits

rare.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms due to abnormal bone structure
searchTerms: nerve compression due to bone shape
tingling caused by abnormal bone structure

rare.symptomName: Skin ulceration over prominent phalangeal areas

imaging: X-ray showing presence of supernumerary phalanx(s) in affected digits
Absence of other skeletal abnormalities on full skeletal survey
genetic: No specific gene mutation identified for isolated hyperphalangy
Genetic testing used primarily to exclude syndromic causes
other: Physical examination revealing digital length discrepancy

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of additional systemic or syndromic features
Genetic mutations associated with syndromic forms
Multiple congenital anomalies beyond isolated digital involvement

redFlags: Presence of multiple congenital anomalies suggesting syndromic diagnosis
Progressive functional impairment or pain in affected digits
references: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Hyperphalangy
Clinical Radiology of Congenital Hand Anomalies, Journal of Hand Surgery
